newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Telecom Eireann to introduce price reduction.
newsitem.headline: Irish Telecom Eireann to introduce price reduction.

text.p: Ireland's Telecom Eireann said on Monday that it will cut the cost to customers of using the telephone by introducing a series of price reductions worth 80 million punts in a full year. Telecom said in a statement that the price cuts would be implemented throughout the coming year.

It said calls to the U.S. and Canada would be reduced by 25 per cent while calls to Britain would fall by 17 per cent at the standard rate to 24 Irish pence per minute, with evening and weekend rates falling by 10 per cent to 22 Irish pence per minute.
Calls to South Africa would be reduced by 38 per cent to 109 Irish pence per minute, Telecom said.

Telecom said the basic telephone connection charge would be reduced by almost a third from 145 to 99 Irish pounds from June 1 and all reconnection charges for existing customers moving house or transferring accounts were being abolished.
This means that a a variety of charges, ranging from 18 to 121 Irish pounds, will no longer exist, it said.
